chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the Qunut in the Witr prayer.

Is there anything fixed to be followed and said? So he (peace be upon him) said: No. Laud upon Allah (Mighty and Majestic) and send Blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and seek Forgiveness for your grievous sin. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Every sin is grievous.

key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: Al-Witr (the odd-numbered prayer concluding the night prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended text for Qunut in Witr prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the flexibility of the Witr Qunut, emphasizing that the supplicant is not bound by a rigid liturgy but should instead focus on praising Allah, sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and seeking forgiveness. The Imam’s concluding remark that 'every sin is grievous' underscores the profound humility required in this voluntary prayer, aligning with the Shia tradition of personal devotion over mechanical recitation. This approach highlights the spiritual depth of the Witr prayer as a moment for intimate communion with God rather than mere ritual performance.
